hints.title: In Place Index Sign Flagging
hints.text: All integers in the array lie between one and n. How can using the values as array indices enable recording visits without additional allocations?

hints.title: Negative Marking Presence Invariant
hints.text: When inspecting absolute value x, negating nums[x - 1] marks x as seen. If nums[x - 1] is already negative, x is a confirmed duplicate.

hints.title: Sign Inversion Duplicate Collector Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty result list. For each element x in the array, compute target index abs(x) minus one. If the value at target index is already negative, append abs(x) to result; otherwise negate the value at target index. Return the result list.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Allocating hash sets or sorting violates the problem explicit requirement of O(1) auxiliary space and O(N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using existing array elements as in-place boolean flags takes O(N) time and requires strictly O(1) auxiliary memory beyond the output.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize index-as-hash-key sign negation and properly use abs() to avoid negative index errors.
